firecrawl_scrape.rationale: It can `Retrieve and extract content from one supplied URL` and return page formats, so attacker-controlled web pages can enter context. The supplied `url` is an agent-chosen destination, and `Browser actions may change the live page` with interactive actions, so it can send data/side effects to a site. SECRET is undetermined because the text does not restrict schemes or network scope; under the least-restrictive reading a supplied URL could be `file://`, localhost, or intranet content that Firecrawl can reach.

firecrawl_map.rationale: It can `Enumerate URLs indexed under one website` and returns `matching URLs`, which a site owner can author. The `url` selects an agent-chosen website, so the request can target an attacker-readable host. SECRET is undetermined because the description does not say the website URL is limited to public internet hosts; it may enumerate non-public reachable sites.

firecrawl_search.rationale: It `Search[es] web, news, or image sources` and developer sources such as `GitHub issues`, `repository READMEs`, and documentation, returning result titles, snippets, descriptions, URLs, and optionally extracted page content. These public and multi-writer sources are attacker-controllable. Queries go to a fixed Firecrawl/search endpoint, so this is not treated as a SINK.

firecrawl_search_feedback.rationale: It records feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` and the response reports refund and `daily-cap status`, which are authenticated team/accounting data. It sends to a fixed Firecrawl endpoint rather than an attacker-chosen destination.

firecrawl_feedback.rationale: It submits feedback for a Firecrawl job and returns `submission status, feedback ID, and accounting fields`, which are non-public account/job data. The destination is the fixed Firecrawl feedback service, not an attacker-chosen host.

firecrawl_crawl.rationale: It starts a crawl at a `website URL` and returns `page data`, so web content can be attacker-controlled. The start URL and `webhook` are agent-chosen destinations, and scrape actions can be interactive. SECRET is undetermined because the text does not restrict the URL to public hosts, so reachable intranet/localhost content is possible under the least-restrictive reading.

firecrawl_check_crawl_status.rationale: It reads `Firecrawl job state` for an `existing crawl ID` and returns `available results`; that job state is non-public account data, and the results can include attacker-authored page content collected by the crawl.

firecrawl_extract.rationale: The deprecated entry point extracts from supplied `urls` and may use web search when URLs are not known, so returned web content is attacker-controllable. The supplied URLs are agent-chosen destinations. SECRET is undetermined because the text does not restrict URL schemes or reachable networks.

firecrawl_agent.rationale: It starts a web research job from a `prompt` and optional `seed URLs`; the agent can `search, navigate, read pages`, so supplied URLs can cause requests to agent-chosen hosts. This call `returns only a job ID`, not the web content itself.

firecrawl_agent_status.rationale: It retrieves progress and `result data` for a `firecrawl_agent` job ID, which is non-public job state. Completed research results may come from searched and read web pages, so they can contain attacker-authored content.

firecrawl_interact.rationale: It can `navigate a page, click controls, fill fields, or run browser code` and `code can run as Bash, Python, or Node`. Because the advertised text does not state that this code is confined to a remote vendor sandbox, HOSTEXEC is kept under the least-restrictive reading, which implies SECRET, UNTRUSTED, and SINK. It also acts on a `live site`, can create `persistent external side effects`, and returns `execution output, stdout/stderr` and session URLs.

firecrawl_interact_stop.rationale: It only stops the live session associated with a `scrapeId` and returns a `success confirmation`; no attacker-controlled content, non-public data, attacker destination, or host execution is advertised.

firecrawl_parse.rationale: It can parse a `filePath` and `Local MCP reads filePath from the server filesystem`, so it can return local file contents, which are SECRET. The threat model does not treat the user's local files as attacker-controlled, and remote web URLs are directed to `firecrawl_scrape`.

firecrawl_monitor_create.rationale: It creates a monitor in the authenticated account and `Returns the created monitor`, which is non-public SaaS data. The monitor `schedules future network checks` and can send `email or webhook notifications`, so page targets, emails, and webhook URLs can deliver data to attacker-readable destinations.

firecrawl_monitor_list.rationale: It lists `monitors for the authenticated account` and returns monitor records and pagination metadata, which are non-public SaaS account data.

firecrawl_monitor_get.rationale: It retrieves one monitor by ID, including `configuration and current state`, from the authenticated account; that is non-public SaaS data.

firecrawl_monitor_update.rationale: It patches an existing account monitor and returns the updated monitor, so it exposes non-public SaaS data. The body can change `targets`, `webhook`, and `notifications`, creating attacker-readable destinations for future checks or notifications.

firecrawl_monitor_delete.rationale: It permanently deletes a monitor by ID in the authenticated account and returns deletion status; existence/status of the account record is non-public SaaS data.

firecrawl_monitor_run.rationale: It queues a check for an account monitor and returns the queued check, which is non-public SaaS job data. It `starts network work for the monitor's configured targets`; SINK is kept because an agent can select a monitor ID whose configured targets were created or updated to attacker-readable destinations, although the destination is indirect through the ID.

firecrawl_monitor_checks.rationale: It lists `historical checks for a monitor` and returns check summaries and pagination metadata for the authenticated account, which are non-public SaaS data.

firecrawl_monitor_check.rationale: It retrieves one monitor check and its `page-level results`; those are non-public account history. Results can include markdown diffs, JSON previous/current values, and a `current snapshot` from monitored web pages, which may be attacker-authored.

firecrawl_research_search_papers.rationale: It searches public scientific sources such as `PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv` and `arXiv` and returns paper titles, authors, and abstracts; paper authors and publishers can control this content.

firecrawl_research_inspect_paper.rationale: It retrieves metadata for an arXiv/PMC/PMID/DOI paper and returns `title, abstract, authors, categories, source IDs, and dates as markdown`; those public paper fields can be author/publisher controlled.

firecrawl_research_related_papers.rationale: It finds citation-graph candidates and returns `ranked candidates`; those candidates are public papers whose titles/authors/metadata can be attacker-authored.

firecrawl_research_read_paper.rationale: It retrieves `in-body passages` from indexed papers; paper full text is public third-party content and can be author-controlled.

firecrawl_research_search_github.rationale: It searches indexed public `GitHub issue, pull-request, and README content` and returns snippets and matched markdown; public GitHub content is multi-writer and attacker-controllable.

firecrawl_developer_search.rationale: It searches developer sources including `GitHub issues`, `merged pull requests`, `repository READMEs`, and documentation, returning URLs, titles, and matched passages; these public/multi-writer sources can be attacker-controlled.

value_conditions.effect: For scrape-style options, the description says this requests `lockdown cache-only retrieval`, which can remove live fetching of the target host for that call, though cached attacker-controlled content may still be returned.

For crawl, the description says `Webhooks and interactive scrape actions are unavailable in safe mode`, reducing those SINK/WRITE routes, though the crawl still starts network work for the configured URL.

notes: All judgements are based only on the advertised descriptions and schemas. Where URL scheme or network reach was not specified, URL-reading tools are treated under the least-restrictive reading for SECRET and marked undetermined.
Search-style query arguments to fixed Firecrawl/vendor endpoints are not treated as SINK destinations.
